cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Back My Version
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When the committee asks about the greenhouse, we were clearing up broken glass. Say that back to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were clearing up after your wheelbarrow hit it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with what we did inside the greenhouse. We don't need the entire approach route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: But if they ask how it broke, I'm telling them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then answer that question when it arrives. First, clearing up. Please stop putting the collision in every opening sentence.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 recruits a repeated cleanup account. A3 corrects B2's ordering as if supervising a statement; A5 responds to B4's honesty limit by directing which question gets which detail.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 adds the collision to A1's rehearsal. A3 narrows the opening, B4 refuses to omit cause if asked, and A5 accommodates truth conditionally while keeping the agreed opening.

relationship.evidence: B2 remembers A's responsibility and B4 refuses to lie about it. A must work with B's ethical limit rather than demand an implausibly willing cover-up.

heightening.evidence: A5's conditional permission to tell the truth is a more strained management tactic than A1's simple repeated version, directly forced by B4.

specificity.evidence: A1 committee and broken greenhouse glass, B2 wheelbarrow impact, and A3 inside cleanup define the event without missing staging.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's repeated opening-sentence instruction serves a rehearsal goal. The approach-route phrase in A3 is a pointed euphemism, not a new plot.

coach2.stated: A1 prepares for committee questions; B2 saw A's wheelbarrow hit glass; B4 will disclose cause if asked.
coach2.inferred: A wants a favorable shared sequence, not necessarily identical false memories.
coach2.missing: No outside committee procedure must be assumed; A imposes their own presentation method.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate; B's resistance makes A's correction specific and consequential.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 repeats A1's account with incriminating cause added.
